rules.title: Broker fee paid only by the party who hired the broker
rules.requirement: A licensed real estate broker or salesperson may contract solely with either a prospective tenant or a landlord (or landlord's agent), and any fee may only be paid by the party who originally engaged and contracted with the broker. A tenant therefore cannot be charged a broker fee for a broker the landlord hired.
rules.key_value: Fee payable only by the party (lessor or tenant) who engaged the broker
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.
rules.coverage_text: Persons engaged in the business of finding dwelling accommodations for prospective tenants for a fee; licensed brokers or salespersons contracting with tenants or landlords for residential rentals.
rules.extraction_note: The rule governs broker fees, a type of upfront tenant charge, not application or screening fees specifically. It is classified under application_screening_fees as the closest category ('allowed upfront charges'), so the classification is uncertain. The effective date of 2025-08-01 comes from the bracketed note on the amended text. The document does not state the enactment date of St. 2025, c. 9, and it does not state a penalty. The prior version, effective until 2025-08-01, only required that fee-charging apartment finders be licensed.
